statement: ABCD is a rectangle with AB = 8 and BC = 6. A point P is chosen anywhere inside it. What is the total area of triangles PAB and PCD?

choices.misconception: I placed P at the centre and found the area of only one of the two triangles.
I placed P at the centre and subtracted one triangle from the rectangle instead of adding the two triangles.
I multiplied base by height for each triangle and forgot to halve.

choices.text: It depends on where P is
choices.misconception: I thought the total changes as P moves, so it cannot be found.

hints: Both triangles have a base of length 8.
The two triangles stand on opposite sides of length 8, and their heights are the distances from P to those two sides. Ask what those two heights always add up to.
The height of PAB plus the height of PCD is always the full height 6 of the rectangle.

solutions.reliable: Triangle PAB has base 8 and height h, the distance from P to AB. Triangle PCD has base 8 and height 6 - h. Their areas add to 8h / 2 + 8(6 - h) / 2 = 8 x 6 / 2 = 24, whatever h is. The transferable idea: when an answer is claimed not to depend on a point, move the point somewhere convenient, or show the varying parts cancel.
solutions.elegant: Draw a line through P parallel to AB. It cuts the rectangle into two smaller rectangles, and each triangle is exactly half of one of them, so together they are half of 48.

whyOnTest: Cutting the rectangle through P shows each triangle is half a piece, a dissection idea that also checks whether you believe the answer can be fixed.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
